name: BERT
description:
Here is how to read the BERT config.json. The architecture class is BertForMaskedLM, which is the transformers (or equivalent) module that wires embeddings, attention, the MLP, and the language-modelling head that turns hidden states into next-token logits.

hidden_size is 768: that is the width of every residual stream vector. The embedding matrix is therefore 30,522 × 768: each token id owns a vector of that width.

num_attention_heads is 12, so each head sees 64 dimensions (768 / 12). The ratio test is hidden_size / num_attention_heads = 768 / 12 = 64. 64 is a multiple of 32 (NVIDIA warp-friendly), and a multiple of 16 (Huawei cube-friendly), and a power of two (Triton / FlashAttention-friendly). From this number alone you cannot name the training chip.

num_hidden_layers is 12: the stack is that many transformer blocks deep.

intermediate_size is 3,072. In a SwiGLU MLP this is the high-dimensional workspace: the 768-wide stream is projected up, activated with gelu, then projected back. Labs usually round this width to a multiple of 128 or 256 so it tiles on the chip.

max_position_embeddings is 512 tokens — the context window in the config. There is no rope_scaling entry, so the rotary positions are used as-is.

vocab_size is 30,522. bos/eos ids, when present, are just two special rows in that table; the padded vocab is often larger than the tokenizer’s real inventory.

The copy of config.json is from https://huggingface.co/google-bert/bert-base-uncased/blob/main/config.json.
